headline: Zyxel zero-day exploited against nearly 1,000 switches; Apple CVE-2024-27834 joins KEV; DreamHost breach details grow

bullets.text: New, critical: BleepingComputer reports Zyxel has fixed a zero-day that was exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches.
New, critical: CISA KEV added CVE-2024-27834, an improper authentication flaw in multiple Apple products, on 2026-11-04, with a federal due date of 2026-11-18.

Developing, DreamHost: TechCrunch reports hackers stole customer files and inboxes during a months-long attack. BleepingComputer says DreamHost confirmed the breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions.
Still active, critical: The Hacker News reports APT29-linked hackers hijacked a web analytics script to deliver iOS and Android exploits. Help Net Security describes the exploits as n-day.
Still active, cPGuard, 4 outlets: SecurityWeek reports malicious updates served in an OpsShield supply chain attack. BleepingComputer says the hijacked autoupdate deployed a backdoor and stole data.

Still active, WordPress Core, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports CISA flags a WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a race condition added 2026-11-03, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.

actions: Apply Zyxel's fix for the exploited zero-day on your network switches and check them for signs of compromise.
Patch Apple devices for CVE-2024-27834 (KEV due 2026-11-18) and keep managed iOS and Android devices on current releases.
If you host at DreamHost, change FTP passwords, end webmail sessions and treat customer files and inboxes as potentially stolen.
Check Debian and Ubuntu advisories for the APT flaw and apply fixed packages on hosts and images as soon as they are available.
If you use mSecure, change the master password and rotate stored credentials. If you run cPGuard, check servers for the backdoor.
Patch WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 (KEV due 2026-11-06) and Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527.
